# QS-CFW-4922-70 - Quality specification - gear blank CFW-4922-70 (8620)

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P2  
Parts: CFW-4922-70

Scope

This quality specification defines acceptance criteria and inspection practices for gear blank CFW-4922-70 manufactured from material grade 8620 at Plant P2. The document applies to all forgings identified by the part designation CFW-4922-70 from receipt of forged blanks through final release for downstream machining. It is intended for use by quality inspectors, production supervisors, and material handling personnel to ensure conformity to key functional and safety-related attributes of the gear blank prior to machining and heat treatment operations.

Background and rationale

CFW-4922-70 is a finished blank geometry intended for carburizing and finishing as a power-transmission gear. Dimensional integrity, bore concentricity, and core hardness are primary drivers for part performance and fit in downstream processes. The acceptance criteria in this document isolate critical attributes that must be verified on each lot to reduce rework, scrap, and assembly issues. The specified hardness band balances machinability for pre-machining operations with sufficient core strength to endure subsequent heat treatment and service loads. The bore tolerance controls runout and fit with mating assemblies; the maximum forging weight controls handling, tooling selection, and process capability of forging equipment.

Requirements table

- Attribute: Hardness
  - Requirement: The hardness range for gear blank CFW-4922-70 (CFW-4922-70) is 38-42 HRC.
  - Applicability: All forgings prior to final release.
  - Acceptance: Within stated hardness range on cross section at the core location specified in drawing.

- Attribute: Bore diameter tolerance
  - Requirement: The bore diameter tolerance for gear blank CFW-4922-70 (CFW-4922-70) is ±0.03 mm.
  - Applicability: Bore features intended for press fit or bearing fit as shown on the part drawing.
  - Acceptance: Measured bore diameter must be within nominal dimension plus or minus the stated tolerance.

- Attribute: Forging weight
  - Requirement: The maximum forging weight for gear blank CFW-4922-70 (CFW-4922-70) is 69.8 kg.
  - Applicability: Individual blank weight as-recorded on material disposition documentation.
  - Acceptance: Any forging exceeding the stated maximum must be segregated and dispositioned as nonconforming.

Inspection method

General

Inspectors shall employ calibrated measurement equipment and documented methods to verify each attribute. All instruments used shall have valid calibration status traceable to the laboratory control system. For each lot, record the instrument identification and operator initials on the inspection record.

Hardness testing

Perform hardness verification on an as-forged cross section representative of the bulk material. Use a hardness tester appropriate for HRC scale with a correctly specified indenter for steel substrates. Prepare the test surface to remove scale and to provide a flat, smooth area sufficient for an accurate indenter reading. Take readings at the core location defined on the engineering drawing for CFW-4922-70. Document individual readings and calculate the observed range for the part sampled. Compare to the requirement in the requirements table. If the sample reading approaches the limits of the range, take additional independent measurements on the same part and on additional parts from the lot to confirm conformance.

Bore diameter measurement

Measure bore diameter using a bore gauge or internal micrometer with calibration certificates on file. Ensure the measuring instrument is zeroed and the part is stabilized at ambient shop conditions prior to measurement. When measuring, take multiple cross-sectional readings at normal intervals around the bore to detect out-of-round conditions. Record the nominal drawing diameter and each measured value on the inspection record. Calculate the deviation from nominal and verify the deviation is within the tolerance stated in the requirements table. For a bore with nonuniform geometry, follow the drawing callouts for the inspection location.

Weight verification

Verify forging weight using scales appropriate for the stated maximum weight. Record the measured weight on the inspection record and compare to the requirement. If the measured weight equals or is less than the stated maximum, forward the part for normal processing. If the measured weight exceeds the stated maximum, follow nonconformance handling procedures.

Records and examples

Inspection records shall include the following for each lot: part designation CFW-4922-70, lot identifier, inspector name or initials, instrument identification and calibration status, hardness readings and locations, bore measurements with locations, measured weight, and final disposition. Example entries are provided in the QMS inspection form template. All records shall be retained in the document control or quality records repository in accordance with company retention policy for traceability to the lot.

Nonconformance handling

Segregation

Any forging that fails to meet a requirement in the requirements table shall be immediately segregated and clearly labeled as nonconforming. Segregated stock shall be stored separate from conforming inventory and access limited to authorized personnel.

Disposition

The quality engineer or designee shall review nonconforming material and determine disposition. Possible dispositions include rework, return to supplier, use-as-is with concession, or scrap. Disposition decisions shall be documented on the nonconformance report and include the specific attribute(s) that failed, measured values, and justification for the selected disposition.

Containment and root cause

For process escapes or repeated nonconformances, containment actions must be initiated to prevent additional nonconforming parts from entering downstream operations. Conduct a root cause analysis involving production, tooling, and materials personnel to identify corrective actions. Implement corrective actions and verify effectiveness with additional inspection records showing compliance to the stated requirements.

Notification and records

Notify affected stakeholders when a lot is dispositioned as nonconforming, including production scheduling and downstream process owners. Maintain nonconformance records including disposition rationale, corrective action plan, and verification evidence in the quality system. The inspection records described above shall be appended to the nonconformance report when applicable.

This specification is the governing acceptance standard for part CFW-4922-70 at Plant P2. Compliance with the stated requirements is mandatory prior to releasing forgings for subsequent processing.
